title: Inquest called into death of Craig McDougall
article: An inquest has been called by the province's chief medical examiner that will look further into the death of a man shot by Winnipeg cops five years ago.

Craig Vincent McDougall, 26, was shot and killed by police in the early morning hours of Aug. 2, 2008 at a Simcoe Street home. Police said McDougall refused to put down a knife at the time he was shot multiple times. He was also struck with a Taser during the incident.

In the weeks following his death, aboriginal leaders claimed the killing was racially motivated and that McDougall had actually been holding a cellphone, not a knife. However, an investigation by Winnipeg police, as well as a review of the case by an outside body, found no wrongdoing on the part of police.

The inquest, which by law must be called when a person dies at the hands of police, will attempt to determine the circumstances relating to McDougall's death and what, if anything, can be done to prevent similar deaths from occurring in the future.
